A used object cannot be dropped before what uses it, and an edit names what it would break; a body is text, so a rename never reaches into it.
what a version of an engine's database has or lacks (a type, a kind of object, an option, a clause), with the first and last version that has it.
the parts of an index, in order: each a column or an expression, ordered or only included.
the versions of their databases the engines support, in order, as each engine declares them.
the columns of a key or a link, in order; for a link, each with the column it refers to.
every design people work on here, each the rows of these tables that point at it: never a database, a schema or a table of its own.
an index of a table, in the order the table lists them.
a line of work: its newest turn. Switching branch moves the design to its newest turn.
what an engine's live read asks a server of each version, what it gives, and the grant it needs.
the columns of a table, a view or a composite type, in order, with what every engine says of a column.
the kinds of object each engine has, as it declares them; an object of a kind its design's engine does not declare is refused.
everything a namespace holds, and what the server holds beside its namespaces: tables, views, routines, triggers, events, sequences, types, tablespaces, whatever kinds the engine declares.
how a table is split into partitions.
an object a choice reads, by its namespace and a name or a pattern, as the server names them; a choice that lists none reads every object of the kinds it lists.
what a turn did, one operation at a time, each of a kind the agent and the canvas name (added table orders).
the partitions of a table, in order, with their bounds; where the engine makes a partition a table of its own, that table.

what a person chose to read from a design's database (decision read-scope): everything, or the kinds of object and the objects listed under it; a choice is never changed, a new choice is a new row, so every read names the choice it ran with.
a locked version of the schema: the log up to one turn, its number and its hash.
every migration applied to schema_forge, by its owner.
a trigger: when it fires, on which changes, for rows or statements, and what it runs.
a view's query, as the server writes it, and what it guarantees of rows written through it.
the value of each field a connection's engine declares, by the field's key; never a field the engine declares secret.
a sequence object, and how it numbers.
one round of work: the agent's answer to one prompt, a person's edit, an import, an undo, a restore. Every change belongs to one; each follows the turn before it, so turns form a tree.
each step of a connection test, in order, and what it said (docs/connections.xml).

the log: every row an operation inserted, updated or deleted, in any table of the cortex and the engines, with its values before and after; appended, never edited. Undo applies them backwards, redo forwards.
the parameters of a routine, in order, as the server reads them: for search and the canvas.
the workspace this database is, exactly one row: its saved connections and every design are in this database.
the tables and columns a custom perspective shows, in order.

props.comment: puts the triggers of every rule view of a namespace on each table the view reads; returns how many tables it guarded
after a write to a table a rule reads, marks the rule to be read again at commit

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION cortex.rule_again()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'pg_catalog'
AS $function$
BEGIN
  PERFORM cortex.rule_marks();
  DELETE FROM pg_temp.rule_marks m WHERE m.rule = TG_ARGV[0];
  RETURN NULL;
END $function$

props.comment: gives an owner's namespace to sf_service (rows, the rules), sf_agent (the design's rows) and sf_reader (reading), so the schema changes only as sf_owner
at commit, refuses the commit when the rule view named by the trigger lists a row; once held, it is not read again until a write marks it; it runs as sf_owner, so no writer can skip it
makes, or checks, the session's table of rules held in this transaction, which only sf_owner writes
props.create:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION cortex.rule_marks()
 RETURNS void
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'pg_catalog'
AS $function$
BEGIN
  -- The marks of the rules read and held in this transaction: a temporary table this function's owner (sf_owner) makes
  -- and alone may write, emptied at every commit. A table of that name another role made first is refused, so no
  -- writer can mark a rule held that was not read.
  CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE IF NOT EXISTS rule_marks (rule text PRIMARY KEY) ON COMMIT DELETE ROWS;
  IF (SELECT c.relowner FROM pg_class c WHERE c.oid = 'pg_temp.rule_marks'::regclass) <> (SELECT oid FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'pg_temp.rule_marks was made by another role: the rules cannot be held' USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege';
  END IF;
END $function$
